color_palette.name: Chrome Slick
color_palette.usage: Primary background surface across all pages — a cool, metallic silver-blue that evokes Y2K chrome finishes; used on the sidebar navigation panel, page backgrounds, and card base layers to unify the glossy digital atmosphere.

color_palette.name: Bubblegum Burst
color_palette.usage: Primary CTA buttons, active navigation states, article category badges, and hero accent highlights — the loudest pop note in the palette, used wherever Pixelwave needs to command immediate attention.

color_palette.name: Laserdisc Lavender
color_palette.usage: Section dividers, hover states on sidebar nav links, feature card borders, and decorative starburst/pill ornaments — bridges the pink and blue poles of the palette with a dreamy digital shimmer.

color_palette.name: Baby Screen Blue
color_palette.usage: Hyperlinks, pull-quote highlights, article tag chips, and the glossy gradient mid-stop on hero panels — evokes the luminous blue of early-2000s LCD screens and browser chrome.

color_palette.name: Void Pixel
color_palette.usage: Primary body text, sidebar navigation text, article headlines at body scale, and the dark anchor strip in the footer — a deep indigo-black that grounds the candy palette without reading as a flat neutral.

color_palette.name: Glosspop White
color_palette.usage: Content panel surfaces, article reading background, and card fill on top of Chrome Slick — a barely-there cool white that keeps long-form text legible while staying within the icy Y2K color temperature.

color_palette.name: Starfield Magenta
color_palette.usage: Eyebrow labels on hero sections, 'NEW' and 'TRENDING' sticker badges, lens-flare decorative spots, and hover glows on CTA buttons — a saturated accent used sparingly for maximum electric pop.

color_palette.name: Foil Silver
color_palette.usage: Metadata text (publish dates, author bylines, read-time labels), inactive sidebar nav items, horizontal rule lines, and image overlay tints — a muted chrome tone that recedes without disappearing.

typography.heading_treatment: Nunito at display weights (800–900) for H1 and H2 headlines — its rounded terminals are quintessentially Y2K bubbly-digital; set in all-caps or title case with very tight tracking (-0.02em to -0.04em) at large sizes (48–96px for hero, 32–48px for section heads) to create the condensed, glossy-billboard energy of early-2000s tech branding. H3 and H4 drop to 700 weight with slightly looser tracking, maintaining the rounded warmth at smaller scales.
typography.body_treatment: Archivo at Regular (400) and Medium (500), 16–18px, line-height 1.65–1.75, for all article body copy, sidebar descriptions, and panel prose — its condensed grotesque structure gives the publication a punchy, editorial density appropriate for a tech magazine, while its clean geometry complements the rounded display heads without competing.
typography.accent_treatment: Montserrat in uppercase with wide letter-spacing (0.12–0.18em) at 10–13px only — reserved strictly for eyebrow labels ('FEATURES', 'TRENDING NOW'), article category chips, badge stickers, metadata bylines, and caption tags. Never used at display or body scale; its geometric rigidity acts as a sharp structural counterpoint to Nunito's softness, reinforcing the Y2K mix of slick tech and bubblegum pop.

pages.page_level_design_instruction:
The Pixelwave Home page is a Y2K Gloss landing experience built on a persistent left sidebar navigation layout. The page runs three sections in a deliberate dense → airy → electric rhythm that prevents any two consecutive sections from feeling structurally identical.

SIDEBAR: A fixed-width left sidebar (240px on desktop, collapsing to a top bar on mobile) sits on a Chrome Slick (#C8D8E8) surface. Navigation labels are set in Montserrat uppercase at 11px with 0.15em tracking in Void Pixel (#1A1040) for inactive items and Laserdisc Lavender (#B8A0E8) for hover states. The Pixelwave wordmark sits at the top of the sidebar in Nunito 900 weight, with "PIXELWAVE" in Bubblegum Burst (#FF6EB4) and the tagline "The Future, Buffering Now." in Foil Silver (#8FA8C0) at 10px Montserrat uppercase beneath it. A thin Laserdisc Lavender horizontal rule separates the wordmark from the nav links. Glossy pill ornaments — small rounded rectangles with a chrome gradient from Glosspop White to Chrome Slick — sit decoratively between nav sections as structural dividers.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The hero section (Section 1) delivers the page's defining visual stunt — the word "GLITCHING" from the headline is set at an enormous display scale (120–140px on desktop), in Nunito 900 all-caps, rendered as a chrome gradient type treatment (left-to-right gradient from Baby Screen Blue #7EC8F0 through Glosspop White #F0F4FF to Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8) that bleeds off the right edge of the content area, deliberately cropped by the viewport. This is a typographic bleed move — the oversized word is not contained within any box or panel; it tears across the full content-column width and exits the frame. A Starfield Magenta (#CC00AA) lens-flare dot (a radial gradient burst, roughly 80px diameter, semi-transparent) overlaps the "G" in GLITCHING, sitting between the type and the background layer. This move is unmistakably Y2K — chrome type, lens flare, oversized display scale — and it is impossible to mistake for modern SaaS. The signature moment lives in Section 1 and sets the entire page's energy.

SECTION SEQUENCE & RHYTHM:
- Section 1 (Hero): Maximum density and vertical drama. Full-bleed Void Pixel (#1A1040) dark panel — the only dark surface on the page — creates maximum contrast against the rest of the page. Asymmetric, type-dominant, with the bleed headline as the signature moment. High energy, low whitespace.
- Section 2 (Article List): Shifts to a Glosspop White (#F0F4FF) surface. A horizontal masthead-strip eyebrow at the top, then three article cards laid out in a 3-column grid — but each card is deliberately non-identical: Card 1 is taller with a category badge sticker overlapping its top-left corner; Card 2 is standard height; Card 3 has a "TRENDING" starburst ornament at its top-right. Cards use Chrome Slick (#C8D8E8) as fill with Laserdisc Lavender (#B8A0E8) borders. Medium density.
- Section 3 (CTA / Newsletter): A saturated Bubblegum Burst (#FF6EB4) full-bleed panel — the loudest color block on the page — with centered composition (justified by the CTA close convention and the need for pop contrast). A glossy pill button and a starburst ornament make this feel electric and conclusive. Low density, high color impact.

COLOR SURFACE LOGIC: Void Pixel dark panel (Section 1) → Glosspop White editorial surface (Section 2) → Bubblegum Burst saturated block (Section 3). No two adjacent sections share a surface color. The Chrome Slick sidebar anchors the left edge throughout. Baby Screen Blue is used expressively in the hero type gradient and as link/tag chip color in Section 2 — not only on CTAs. Starfield Magenta appears as the lens-flare ornament in Section 1 and as the "TRENDING" badge in Section 2.

TYPOGRAPHY HIERARCHY: Hero H1 at 120–140px Nunito 900 all-caps (bleed treatment). Section 2 headline at 36px Nunito 800. Section 3 headline at 48px Nunito 900 centered. Body copy in Archivo 400 at 16–17px, line-height 1.7. All eyebrow labels in Montserrat uppercase 11px, 0.15em tracking. Article card titles in Nunito 700 at 20px. Metadata in Foil Silver (#8FA8C0) Montserrat 10px uppercase.

DENSITY / WHITESPACE: Section 1 is intentionally compressed vertically (tight padding, type fills the panel). Section 2 has generous card gutters (24px) and breathing room above/below the grid. Section 3 is sparse — large padding, single CTA, centered — acting as a visual exhale before the footer.

RESPONSIVE BEHAVIOR: On tablet (768–1024px), sidebar collapses to a top navigation bar; hero headline scales to 72–80px; article cards stack to 2 columns. On mobile (<768px), single-column layout; hero headline at 48–56px with bleed still active (word exits right edge); article cards stack to 1 column; sidebar becomes a hamburger drawer. The signature bleed move is preserved at all breakpoints — the word always exits the right edge of the content column.

section_design_plans.nl_prompt:
SECTION 1 — HERO. Full-bleed Void Pixel (#1A1040) dark panel spanning the entire content column width (right of the sidebar). Padding: 80px top, 64px bottom, 48px left, 0px right (intentionally no right padding to allow the headline bleed). No image asset — this is a pure typographic hero.

LAYOUT: Single-column, left-aligned text stack, but the headline itself breaks the column grid.

EYEBROW: 'NOW LOADING' — Montserrat uppercase, 11px, 0.15em letter-spacing, Starfield Magenta (#CC00AA) color. Sits 0px above the headline with a 2px Starfield Magenta left border acting as an eyebrow rule (8px tall, 2px wide, flush left). No pill background — just the colored text and rule.

HEADLINE TREATMENT (SIGNATURE MOMENT): The headline 'The Future Is Already Glitching' is split into two typographic tiers. Line 1: 'THE FUTURE IS ALREADY' — Nunito 900, all-caps, 52px, Glosspop White (#F0F4FF), left-aligned, tight tracking (-0.03em), contained within the column. Line 2: 'GLITCHING' — Nunito 900, all-caps, 130px on desktop (scales to 72px tablet / 48px mobile), rendered with a left-to-right horizontal gradient fill: Baby Screen Blue (#7EC8F0) at 0% → Glosspop White (#F0F4FF) at 50% → Laserdisc Lavender (#B8A0E8) at 100%. This word bleeds off the right edge of the content area — it is NOT clipped by a container; overflow is visible and the word exits the viewport right edge. Tracking: -0.04em. This is the page's signature moment.

LENS FLARE ORNAMENT: A Starfield Magenta (#CC00AA) radial gradient burst, approximately 80px diameter, 60% opacity, sits overlapping the top-left of the letter 'G' in 'GLITCHING' — positioned at the intersection of Line 1 and Line 2, slightly above the baseline of Line 2. It is a decorative layer behind the text (z-index below type) so the type reads through the glow. This is a Y2K lens-flare visual cue, grounded directly in the aesthetic.

SUBHEADLINE: 'Pixelwave covers the technology trends, digital culture shifts, and breakthrough ideas that everyone will be talking about tomorrow.' — Archivo 400, 17px, line-height 1.7, Foil Silver (#8FA8C0), left-aligned, max-width 520px. 28px margin-top from the headline block.

CTA BUTTONS: Two CTAs side by side, left-aligned, 32px margin-top from subheadline. CTA 1 'Read the Latest Issue': glossy pill button — Bubblegum Burst (#FF6EB4) background with a top-highlight gloss effect (a subtle white-to-transparent linear gradient overlay on the top half of the pill), Void Pixel (#1A1040) label text, Nunito 700, 15px, all-caps, horizontal padding 28px, vertical padding 12px, border-radius 999px. CTA 2 'Explore the Archive': ghost pill button — transparent background, 2px Laserdisc Lavender (#B8A0E8) border, Laserdisc Lavender label text, same font specs, same sizing. 16px gap between the two buttons.

A thin horizontal rule in Laserdisc Lavender (#B8A0E8) at 1px, 40% opacity, spans the full content column width at the very bottom of the section, acting as a structural divider into Section 2.

SECTION 2 — ARTICLE LIST (TRENDING STORIES). Surface: Glosspop White (#F0F4FF) background. Padding: 56px top, 64px bottom, 48px left, 48px right.

MASTPHEAD STRIP: At the very top of the section, a full-width horizontal strip in Chrome Slick (#C8D8E8), 44px tall, contains the eyebrow label 'TOP STORIES' on the left (Montserrat uppercase, 11px, 0.15em tracking, Void Pixel #1A1040) and the section headline 'What's Trending on Pixelwave' on the right (Nunito 800, 18px, Void Pixel #1A1040, right-aligned). This masthead-strip treatment replaces the standard eyebrow → headline vertical stack, creating a horizontal editorial band that feels like a magazine section header. The strip has no border-radius — flat, full-width, flush to the section edges. 24px margin-bottom from the strip to the card grid.

CARD GRID: Three article cards in a 3-column grid, 24px column gap, equal width. Cards share Chrome Slick (#C8D8E8) fill and a 1.5px Laserdisc Lavender (#B8A0E8) border, border-radius 12px. Each card has 24px internal padding. Cards are deliberately non-identical in ornament treatment:

CARD 1 — 'The AI Chip War Nobody Is Talking About': A glossy pill badge sticker in Bubblegum Burst (#FF6EB4) with 'AI & HARDWARE' in Montserrat uppercase 9px Void Pixel text overlaps the top-left corner of the card, rotated -4 degrees, sitting half-outside the card border (this is the overlapping sticker move from the Y2K aesthetic — it breaks the card boundary). Card height is slightly taller than Cards 2 and 3 (add 32px extra bottom padding) to give it visual hierarchy as the lead story. Title: Nunito 700, 20px, Void Pixel (#1A1040), tight tracking -0.02em, 2 lines max. Description: Archivo 400, 15px, line-height 1.65, Void Pixel (#1A1040) at 80% opacity. Metadata row at bottom: '7 MIN READ' in Foil Silver (#8FA8C0) Montserrat uppercase 10px, with a Baby Screen Blue (#7EC8F0) dot separator (4px circle) between category and read-time.

CARD 2 — 'Gen Z Is Rebuilding the Social Web — Again': Standard height. Category chip 'DIGITAL CULTURE' as an inline pill — Baby Screen Blue (#7EC8F0) background, Void Pixel (#1A1040) text, Montserrat uppercase 9px, border-radius 999px, 6px vertical / 10px horizontal padding — sits inside the card at the top, no rotation, no overflow. Title and description same font specs as Card 1. Metadata: '5 MIN READ' in Foil Silver (#8FA8C0).

CARD 3 — 'Why Every Startup Suddenly Wants to Be an OS': A Starfield Magenta (#CC00AA) starburst ornament — an 8-point star shape, approximately 48px diameter — sits at the top-right corner of the card, overlapping the card border, with 'TRENDING' in Montserrat uppercase 8px Glosspop White (#F0F4FF) centered inside the starburst. This is a direct Y2K starburst visual cue used as a structural badge. Category chip 'STARTUPS' as an inline pill in Laserdisc Lavender (#B8A0E8) background, Void Pixel text. Title and description same specs. Metadata: '6 MIN READ' in Foil Silver.

SECTION CTA: 'See All Features' — right-aligned below the card grid, 32px margin-top. Rendered as a text link with a Baby Screen Blue (#7EC8F0) underline (2px, offset 3px), Nunito 700, 15px, Baby Screen Blue text, with a right-pointing chevron (→) in Bubblegum Burst (#FF6EB4) immediately after the label. No button pill — this is a directional editorial link, not a primary CTA, keeping the section from over-buttoning.

RESPONSIVE: On tablet, 2-column grid (Cards 1 and 2 in row 1, Card 3 full-width in row 2). On mobile, 1-column stacked cards, sticker overlaps preserved.

SECTION 3 — CTA / NEWSLETTER SUBSCRIPTION. Surface: Full-bleed Bubblegum Burst (#FF6EB4) panel — the loudest and most saturated color block on the page. This is the electric color-block move that closes the page. Padding: 72px top, 72px bottom, 48px left, 48px right. Centered composition (justified here: CTA close convention + maximum pop symmetry demanded by the Y2K aesthetic's bubblegum energy).

DECORATIVE LAYER: Two large glossy pill ornaments — elongated rounded rectangles, approximately 200px wide × 48px tall, with a chrome gradient fill (Glosspop White at top to Chrome Slick at bottom, 40% opacity) — are positioned behind the text content: one in the upper-left quadrant of the section (rotated 15 degrees) and one in the lower-right quadrant (rotated -10 degrees). These are not interactive; they are Y2K gloss pill ornaments used as structural decoration. They sit at z-index below all text.

EYEBROW: 'STAY PLUGGED IN' — Montserrat uppercase, 11px, 0.15em tracking, Starfield Magenta (#CC00AA) color. Centered. 0px margin-bottom (tight to headline).

HEADLINE: 'Get Pixelwave in Your Inbox Every Week' — Nunito 900, 48px, all-caps, Void Pixel (#1A1040), centered, tight tracking -0.03em. Line-height 1.1. Max-width 640px, centered. This is the largest type on a non-dark surface on the page — its weight against the Bubblegum Burst background creates a high-contrast pop moment.

SUBHEADLINE: 'No algorithm. No noise. Just the sharpest technology stories, curated and delivered every Tuesday.' — Archivo 400, 17px, line-height 1.7, Void Pixel (#1A1040) at 85% opacity, centered, max-width 480px. 20px margin-top from headline.

EMAIL INPUT + CTA ROW: 32px margin-top from subheadline. A horizontal pill-shaped input+button combo, max-width 460px, centered. The input field: Glosspop White (#F0F4FF) background, no visible border (the pill shape contains both elements), border-radius 999px on the left half, placeholder text 'Your email address' in Foil Silver (#8FA8C0) Archivo 400 15px, 20px left padding. The submit button 'Subscribe Free': attached directly to the right end of the input (no gap), Void Pixel (#1A1040) background, Glosspop White (#F0F4FF) label text, Nunito 700, 14px, all-caps, border-radius 999px on the right half, 24px horizontal padding, 14px vertical padding. The combined pill has a 3px Void Pixel (#1A1040) outer border and a subtle top-highlight gloss overlay (white to transparent, 30% opacity, top half only) — the glossy pill treatment from the Y2K visual cues applied to the form itself.

DISCLAIMER MICRO-TEXT: 'Free forever. Unsubscribe anytime.' — Montserrat uppercase, 9px, 0.12em tracking, Void Pixel (#1A1040) at 50% opacity, centered, 12px margin-top from the input row.

RESPONSIVE: On mobile, the input and button stack vertically (input full-width, button full-width below it, both with border-radius 999px independently). Headline scales to 32px. Glossy pill ornaments scale down to 120px wide and remain in corners.

pages.page_level_design_instruction:
The Features page for Pixelwave operates as the editorial heart of the publication — a dense, confident, Y2K-charged listing page that rewards browsing while communicating curatorial authority. The sidebar navigation (fixed left, ~240px wide, Chrome Slick #C8D8E8 surface with Void Pixel #1A1040 nav text and Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8 hover states) persists across the full page height. The main content area sits to the right of the sidebar and carries all three sections in sequence.

SECTION RHYTHM: The page deliberately avoids uniform section skeletons. Section 1 (page_header) is a masthead-style full-bleed chromatic statement — dense, typographically dominant, asymmetric. Section 2 (item_grid) is the content-heavy workhorse — a structured editorial grid with expressive card treatments and Y2K ornamental detailing. Section 3 (cta) is a compact, punchy close — a saturated magenta-pink pill-shaped band rather than a standard centered CTA block. The rhythm moves: LOUD → DENSE → SHARP, creating deliberate alternation between spectacle, information, and action.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The signature moment lives in Section 1 and is a typographic stunt — the headline "Big Ideas. Sharp Takes. No Filler." is set in Nunito 900 weight at approximately 88–96px, all-caps, with tracking at -0.04em, in Glosspop White #F0F4FF, laid over a full-bleed chrome gradient panel (Chrome Slick #C8D8E8 to Baby Screen Blue #7EC8F0 to Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8, sweeping diagonally left-to-right). The word "NO FILLER." breaks from the left-aligned block and is set in Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4, creating a dramatic mid-sentence color switch that reads as a visual starburst moment. A large decorative lens-flare circle (semi-transparent Glosspop White, ~320px diameter, low opacity ~15%) bleeds off the top-right corner of the panel, partially crossing into the sidebar zone. This is unmistakably Y2K — chrome + bubblegum + oversized display type with a mid-sentence color explosion is exactly the aesthetic's visual DNA.

COLOR SURFACE LOGIC: Section 1 uses the diagonal chrome gradient as its full-bleed background. Section 2 sits on Glosspop White #F0F4FF for maximum legibility of the editorial grid. Section 3 uses a full-width Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4 band — a saturated color block that breaks the page's cool temperature and lands as a pop exclamation point. The sidebar itself remains Chrome Slick throughout. Foil Silver #8FA8C0 is used for metadata, dividers, and rule lines throughout. Starfield Magenta #CC00AA appears on the 'FEATURES' eyebrow in Section 1 and on 'NEW'/'TRENDING' badge stickers on cards in Section 2.

TYPOGRAPHY HIERARCHY: Nunito 900 all-caps dominates Section 1 hero type. Section 2 card titles use Nunito 700 at 22–24px. Section 3 headline uses Nunito 800 at 36px in Glosspop White against the pink band. Montserrat uppercase 11px with 0.14em tracking handles all eyebrow labels, category chips, and metadata. Archivo 400/500 at 16px handles card descriptions.

DENSITY LOGIC: Section 1 is sparse and typographically dominant — the headline IS the content. Section 2 is the densest zone — six cards in a 2-column grid with rich metadata, category badges, and read-time chips. Section 3 returns to sparse — one headline, one subheadline, one CTA pill, all centered within the color band.

RESPONSIVE BEHAVIOR: On tablet, the sidebar collapses to an icon rail. The Section 2 grid drops from 2 columns to 1 column. Section 1 headline scales down to ~60px. Section 3 band maintains full width. On mobile, the sidebar becomes a top hamburger menu. All sections stack vertically at full width.

section_design_plans.nl_prompt: SECTION 1 — PAGE HEADER (Masthead Typographic Stunt / Signature Moment). This section is a full-bleed chromatic header panel spanning the full width of the content area (right of the sidebar), with no internal padding cap — the gradient bleeds edge-to-edge. Background: a diagonal linear gradient sweeping from top-left to bottom-right — Chrome Slick #C8D8E8 → Baby Screen Blue #7EC8F0 → Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8 — creating a shimmering, iridescent chrome-foil surface that is the visual signature of Y2K gloss. The panel height is approximately 420px on desktop. A large decorative lens-flare circle — semi-transparent Glosspop White #F0F4FF at 12% opacity, approximately 340px in diameter — is positioned so its center sits at the top-right corner of the content panel, bleeding partially off the top edge and partially into the sidebar zone, reinforcing the Y2K aesthetic of light artifacts that ignore grid boundaries. A second smaller lens-flare dot (80px, Glosspop White at 18% opacity) sits at roughly 70% across / 80% down the panel, suggesting a secondary light bounce. These are decorative, behind all text. Content is left-aligned, starting at 48px from the left edge of the content area, vertically centered in the panel with top padding of 64px. Eyebrow label: 'FEATURES' in Montserrat uppercase, 11px, letter-spacing 0.16em, Starfield Magenta #CC00AA — sits 64px from top, left-aligned. Below the eyebrow, 16px gap, the headline occupies two lines: Line 1 — 'BIG IDEAS. SHARP TAKES.' in Nunito 900 weight, all-caps, approximately 88px, tracking -0.04em, color Glosspop White #F0F4FF, left-aligned. Line 2 — 'NO FILLER.' in the exact same font, weight, size, and tracking, but colored Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4 — this mid-sentence color switch IS the signature moment, a visual starburst of editorial attitude that lands like a pop-art punchline. The two lines have 8px line gap between them (tighter than normal to compress them into a single typographic mass). Below the headline, 24px gap, the subheadline: 'Every feature is a deep dive into the technology trend, company, or cultural shift that's actually worth your time.' in Archivo 400, 18px, line-height 1.65, Void Pixel #1A1040 at 85% opacity (slightly softened against the gradient), max-width 560px, left-aligned. No CTA in this section — the headline IS the call to presence. A thin horizontal rule in Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8 at 1.5px runs the full width of the content area at the very bottom of the panel, acting as the ornamental divider before the grid section.

SECTION 2 — ITEM GRID (Editorial Feature Grid). Background: Glosspop White #F0F4FF — a clean, cool-white surface that provides maximum legibility contrast for the six editorial cards. The section sits directly below the Section 1 divider rule. Top padding: 56px. Bottom padding: 64px. Horizontal padding: 48px from the content area edges. Section header block at top: eyebrow 'THIS ISSUE' in Montserrat uppercase, 11px, tracking 0.14em, Baby Screen Blue #7EC8F0, left-aligned. Below it, 12px gap, headline 'Current Features' in Nunito 800, 38px, title-case, tracking -0.02em, Void Pixel #1A1040, left-aligned. A decorative glossy pill ornament — a horizontal rounded rectangle approximately 80px wide × 10px tall, filled with a horizontal gradient from Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4 to Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8 — sits inline to the right of the headline, vertically centered with it, 16px gap from the headline text, as a Y2K starburst/pill accent. Below the headline block, 40px gap, the six cards are laid out in a 2-column grid with 24px column gap and 24px row gap, filling the content area width. Each card: background Glosspop White #F0F4FF, border 1.5px solid Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8, border-radius 12px, padding 28px, no drop shadow (flat glossy aesthetic). Card top: a category badge chip — Montserrat uppercase, 10px, tracking 0.14em, Void Pixel #1A1040 text on a Baby Screen Blue #7EC8F0 pill background (border-radius 999px, padding 4px 10px). The first card ('The AI Chip War Nobody Is Talking About') additionally carries a 'TRENDING' sticker badge — a small Starfield Magenta #CC00AA filled pill with Glosspop White text, Montserrat 9px uppercase, positioned at the top-right corner of the card, slightly overlapping the card border edge (4px outside), reinforcing the Y2K sticker-layering aesthetic. The second card ('Gen Z Is Rebuilding the Social Web') carries a 'NEW' sticker badge in the same style. Below the category chip, 12px gap, card title in Nunito 700, 22px, title-case, tracking -0.01em, Void Pixel #1A1040, left-aligned. Below the title, 10px gap, card description in Archivo 400, 15px, line-height 1.7, Void Pixel #1A1040 at 75% opacity, left-aligned. Below the description, 16px gap, a thin 1px horizontal rule in Foil Silver #8FA8C0 spanning the full card inner width. Below the rule, 12px gap, metadata row: read-time label in Montserrat uppercase, 10px, tracking 0.12em, Foil Silver #8FA8C0, left-aligned (e.g., '7 MIN READ'). On the right side of the metadata row, a text link 'Read Feature →' in Archivo 500, 14px, Baby Screen Blue #7EC8F0, right-aligned, that acts as the per-card CTA. Below the full grid, 40px gap, a centered primary CTA button: label 'Read a Feature' in Montserrat uppercase, 12px, tracking 0.14em, Glosspop White #F0F4FF text, on a Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4 pill background (border-radius 999px, padding 14px 40px). On hover, the button background shifts to Starfield Magenta #CC00AA with a subtle glow. The button is centered in the content area.

SECTION 3 — CTA (Saturated Pop Close Band). This section is a full-width horizontal band — spanning the full width of the content area with zero horizontal padding on the band itself — filled solidly with Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4. This is a deliberate, saturated color block that breaks the cool chrome/white temperature of the page above and lands as a pop-art exclamation point, consistent with the Y2K palette's loudest accent. The band height is approximately 260px on desktop. All content inside is centered both horizontally and vertically within the band. At the very top of the band, a decorative starburst ornament — a small eight-pointed star shape approximately 28px, in Starfield Magenta #CC00AA — sits centered, 32px from the top edge of the band, acting as a Y2K decorative marker before the text. Below the starburst, 12px gap, eyebrow label: 'DIG DEEPER' in Montserrat uppercase, 11px, tracking 0.18em, Void Pixel #1A1040 at 70% opacity, centered. Below the eyebrow, 14px gap, headline: 'Looking for Something Specific?' in Nunito 800, 36px, title-case, tracking -0.02em, Glosspop White #F0F4FF, centered. Below the headline, 12px gap, subheadline: 'Browse every story Pixelwave has ever published in our fully searchable archive.' in Archivo 400, 17px, line-height 1.65, Glosspop White #F0F4FF at 88% opacity, centered, max-width 480px, centered in the band. Below the subheadline, 28px gap, CTA button: label 'Go to the Archive' in Montserrat uppercase, 12px, tracking 0.14em, Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4 text on a Glosspop White #F0F4FF pill background (border-radius 999px, padding 14px 40px, no border). This inverts the button color logic from Section 2 — white pill on pink band vs. pink pill on white background — creating a deliberate Y2K color-flip moment. On hover, the button background shifts to Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8 with Glosspop White text. A second small starburst ornament in Glosspop White #F0F4FF at 40% opacity, approximately 20px, sits centered at the bottom of the band, 24px from the bottom edge, mirroring the top starburst and framing the band as a self-contained decorative unit.

pages.page_level_design_instruction:
The Article page for Pixelwave is a long-form reading experience that never lets the Y2K Gloss aesthetic go quiet — chrome gradients, glossy pills, starbursts, and lens-flare ornaments are structural devices threaded through every section, not decorative afterthoughts. The page uses the sidebar-navigation layout family: a fixed left sidebar (approximately 240px wide on desktop) housing the persistent Pixelwave navigation persists across the full scroll, leaving the right ~75% of the viewport as the reading column. pages.page_level_design_instruction:
**Pixelwave Archive Page — Full Visual Design Direction**

**Page Role & Rhythm Overview**
The Archive page is a dense, browsable index — a living library of Pixelwave's editorial history. The page uses the sidebar navigation layout family: a persistent left sidebar (approximately 240px wide, Chrome Slick #C8D8E8 background, Void Pixel #1A1040 nav text at Archivo Medium 14px) anchors every scroll position, while the main content area occupies the remaining width. The three content sections follow a deliberately varied skeleton — masthead-style page header → topic-grid with a glossy pill/chip system → dense reverse-chronological article index — so no two sections share the same compositional logic.

**Signature Moment — The Chrome Marquee Title Blast**
The page's signature moment lives in Section 1 (page_header). The headline "Every Story We've Ever Told" is set in Nunito 900 weight at an enormous display scale (clamp between 72px and 108px), rendered in a horizontal chrome gradient — a left-to-right sweep from Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8 through Glosspop White #F0F4FF to Baby Screen Blue #7EC8F0 — applied as a CSS text gradient fill. The headline is allowed to overflow its comfortable text column and push toward the right edge of the viewport, deliberately cropping the last word slightly off the right margin on desktop (a Y2K billboard bleed effect). Flanking the headline on the left, a vertical stack of three starburst ornaments in Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4 and Starfield Magenta #CC00AA (alternating, approximately 24px each) acts as a decorative structural spine — not tucked into a corner but sitting flush against the left content column edge, crossing the section's top padding boundary. This is unmistakably Y2K: oversized chrome display type bleeding off-grid, starburst punctuation, candy-pop accent ornaments. No other aesthetic would produce this exact move.

**Color & Surface Logic Across the Page**
- Section 1 (page_header): Full-width Void Pixel #1A1040 dark panel — the only dark-background section on the page, creating maximum contrast entry drama. The chrome gradient headline and Bubblegum Burst starbursts pop against the dark field.
- Section 2 (feature_grid): Glosspop White #F0F4FF content panel surface. Category cards use Chrome Slick #C8D8E8 base with Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8 borders and Baby Screen Blue #7EC8F0 story-count chips. Hover states shift card borders to Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4 with a subtle inner glow.
- Section 3 (article_list): Chrome Slick #C8D8E8 background, creating a cool metallic tray feel. Article rows alternate between Glosspop White #F0F4FF card surfaces and the Chrome Slick background itself, producing a dense editorial ledger rhythm. Category badges use Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4. Issue labels use Foil Silver #8FA8C0.

**Typography Hierarchy**
- Page header H1: Nunito 900, 72–108px, chrome gradient fill, tight tracking (-0.03em), all-caps considered but title case used to keep readability at the bleed scale.
- Section eyebrows: Montserrat uppercase, 11px, 0.15em letter-spacing, Starfield Magenta #CC00AA.
- Section H2 headlines: Nunito 800, 36–48px, Void Pixel #1A1040 on light sections, Glosspop White #F0F4FF on dark section.
- Category card titles: Nunito 700, 20px, Void Pixel #1A1040.
- Card descriptions: Archivo Regular 400, 14px, Foil Silver #8FA8C0, line-height 1.65.
- Story count chips: Montserrat uppercase, 10px, 0.14em tracking, Baby Screen Blue #7EC8F0 text on Chrome Slick pill background.
- Article list titles: Nunito 700, 22px, Void Pixel #1A1040, hover color shifts to Bubblegum Burst #FF6EB4.
- Article descriptions: Archivo Regular 400, 15px, Foil Silver #8FA8C0, line-height 1.7.
- Metadata (category, issue, read time): Montserrat uppercase, 10px, 0.14em tracking, Foil Silver #8FA8C0 with category badge in Bubblegum Burst pill.

**Density & Whitespace Logic**
Section 1 is sparse and dramatic — generous vertical padding (80px top, 64px bottom) with the oversized headline dominating the vertical space. Section 2 is medium-density — a 3-column grid of category cards with 24px gaps and 48px vertical padding. Section 3 is the densest — a full-width article ledger with 16px row padding, horizontal rules in Laserdisc Lavender #B8A0E8, and tightly stacked metadata rows. This dense → sparse → dense oscillation is replaced here by sparse → medium → dense, which builds editorial depth as the reader scrolls.

**Responsive Behavior**
- Sidebar collapses to a top hamburger drawer below 768px; the main content goes full-width.
- Section 1 headline scales down to 52px on tablet, 38px on mobile; the off-grid bleed is removed on mobile (headline wraps normally within padding).
- Section 2 grid collapses: 3 columns → 2 columns at tablet → 1 column at mobile.
- Section 3 article rows stack vertically on mobile with metadata moving below the title/description block.

**Cross-Page Fit**
The Archive page is the densest, most index-like page in the Pixelwave system. Its dark entry panel (Section 1) echoes the hero drama of the Home page but serves a library-framing purpose rather than a story-hook purpose. The category grid in Section 2 visually rhymes with the feature grid on the Features page but uses a different card anatomy (pill chips, story counts). The article ledger in Section 3 is unique to this page — no other page uses a ruled-row index format, making the Archive feel like a proper editorial back-catalog rather than a repeated listing template.

Section 2 (story_block) is the densest, most editorial section — a two-column asymmetric layout with a wide prose column and a narrow decorative column carrying Y2K ornamental elements, giving the page a magazine-feature feeling. Section 3 (item_grid) returns to a lighter, more open density — a three-card team grid with glossy pill badges and a CTA strip, closing the page with warmth and momentum.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The page's signature moment lives in Section 1 — the headline "We Cover the Future So You Don't Get Left Behind" is set in Nunito 900 weight at an enormous display scale (minimum 72px, scaling to 96px on wide viewports), rendered in a chrome gradient treatment (silver-to-baby-blue horizontal gradient across the letterforms, referencing the palette's Chrome Slick and Baby Screen Blue), and positioned flush-left against the sidebar edge so the text bleeds toward the right viewport edge, deliberately overshooting the comfortable content column. A Starfield Magenta (#CC00AA) starburst ornament — a classic Y2K decorative device — is layered OVER the headline text, partially obscuring the word "Future," creating the aesthetic's signature layered, pop-digital energy. This move is unmistakably Y2K Gloss: chrome type, starburst overlay, oversized scale, and deliberate grid-bleeding all trace directly to the aesthetic's visual cues.

COLOR LOGIC: Section 1 uses a Chrome Slick-to-Baby Screen Blue diagonal gradient as the full-bleed panel background, with the sidebar remaining its own Chrome Slick surface. Section 2 uses Glosspop White (#F0F4FF) as the main content panel surface, with a narrow Laserdisc Lavender (#B8A0E8) left-border rule on the prose column and a Void Pixel dark decorative column on the right side of the asymmetric split. Section 3 uses Chrome Slick (#C8D8E8) as the background, with Glosspop White card fills, Bubblegum Burst (#FF6EB4) CTA button, and Laserdisc Lavender card borders.

TYPOGRAPHY: H1 in Section 1 is Nunito 900, 72–96px, tight tracking (-0.03em), chrome gradient fill, title case. H2 in Section 2 is Nunito 800, 36px, Void Pixel, title case. H2 in Section 3 is Nunito 800, 32px, Void Pixel. Eyebrow labels throughout are Montserrat uppercase, 11px, 0.15em letter-spacing, Starfield Magenta. Body prose in Section 2 is Archivo 400, 17px, line-height 1.7, Void Pixel. Team card titles are Nunito 700, 18px; descriptions are Archivo 400, 15px, Foil Silver (#8FA8C0); beat badges are Montserrat uppercase, 10px, Baby Screen Blue chip on Chrome Slick.

RESPONSIVE BEHAVIOR: On wide viewports (≥1280px), the left sidebar is 240px fixed, content area fills the remainder. Section 1 headline scales to 96px. Section 2 is a true two-column asymmetric split (prose at 65%, ornamental column at 35%). Section 3 team cards are three columns. On mid viewports (768–1279px), sidebar collapses to icon rail or top hamburger, Section 2 becomes single-column with the ornamental column stacked below, Section 3 becomes two columns. On mobile (≤767px), all sections stack to single column, Section 1 headline drops to 48px but retains the chrome gradient treatment, starburst scales down proportionally, team cards stack to single column.

The page fits the shared design system by using all established color tokens in their defined roles, maintaining Nunito/Archivo/Montserrat typographic hierarchy, and extending the sidebar navigation pattern. It distinguishes itself from other pages by its editorial intimacy, the chrome-gradient headline stunt, and the asymmetric story-block layout that no other page in the site uses.
